why: Fix the center and the best star around it is greedy: add the k largest neighbour values but only those that are positive. Try every node as center; total work is the sum of degrees.
hints: If you already knew which node was the center, which arms would you pick?
For a fixed center, take its neighbours' values in descending order, stopping after k arms or at the first non-positive value, since arms are optional and a negative arm only lowers the sum.
Build per-node lists of neighbour values; for each node sort (or heapq.nlargest(k, ...)) and sum the positive top k plus the center's own value. Max over all nodes. O(E log E).
pitfalls: The center is always included, even if its value is negative; the answer can be negative.
Arms are optional: skip negative and zero neighbour values.
k = 0 means the star is just the center.
Isolated nodes are valid one-node stars.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ g_nodes ≤ 10^5; 0 ≤ g_edges ≤ 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • -10^4 ≤ values[i] ≤ 10^4 (not stated in the source; values may be negative)
  • 0 ≤ k ≤ g_nodes - 1
  • No self-loops or duplicate edges.
